wars.name: Pyrrhus in Sicily

zones.text: Eryx and the cities that defected

wars.outcome: Pyrrhus lifted the siege of Syracuse (278), took Eryx (277), demanded Carthage 'abandon all of Sicily', failed at Lilybaeum after two months (276) and left; Carthage kept Lilybaeum.
wars.note: The page does not give the year of his departure.

wars.name: First Punic War

zones.text: western Sicily: Akragas, Panormus, Selinous, Heraclea Minoa, Lilybaeum, Drepana, Eryx
Aspis and Tunis, held by Regulus 256-255

wars.outcome: Rome took Akragas (261), Panormus (254) and the hold-outs of the west (252); Carthage held only Lilybaeum and Drepana by 248, Eryx from 247; after the Aegates Islands (241) 'Carthage evacuated Sicily' and paid 3,200 talents. Rome then seized Sardinia and Corsica (237/238).
wars.note: Page dates differ inside the article: Akragas 262 in the lead and 261 in the body; the Carthaginian recapture 255 or 254.

wars.name: Mercenary War

zones.text: Tunis, Utica, Hippo and Leptis Parva, the rebel-held ground

wars.outcome: About 20,000 unpaid soldiers mutinied, the Libyan towns rose, Utica and Hippo killed their garrisons (239); Hamilcar Barca won at the Bagradas, the Saw and Leptis Parva (238) and the revolt was over 'by the winter of 238 BC'. The Sardinian garrisons also mutinied (about 240, History of Sardinia page, which dates no change of ruler then); the island and Corsica passed to Rome in 237 (ledger).
wars.note: The Ancient Carthage page dates the war 241-237; the Hamilcar Barca page c. 240-238.

wars.name: Barcid conquest of Iberia

zones.text: the Guadalquivir valley and the Sierra Morena

wars.outcome: Hamilcar landed at Gades (237), subdued the Turdetani and the area to Cape Nao and founded Akra Leuke (c. 235); he died in 228; Hasdrubal the Fair succeeded him; the Ebro Treaty (226) set the Ebro as the northern limit; Hannibal took Saguntum in 219.
wars.note: Hasdrubal's founding of Carthago Nova (c. 228) and the 221-220 conquests of the Meseta are not on the pages opened.

wars.name: Second Punic War
wars.outcome: Rome expelled Carthage from Iberia (Carthago Nova 209, Baecula 208, Ilipa and Gades 206), Hannibal left Italy, and Scipio won at Zama (October 202). The treaty accepted in spring 201 stripped Carthage of its overseas territories and some African land, made it pay 10,000 talents over 50 years, left it ten warships and barred war outside Africa.

wars.name: Carthaginian-Numidian war of 151 BC
wars.outcome: Carthage counter-attacked Masinissa despite the 201 treaty; its army was beaten at Oroscopa and surrendered; Rome used the breach as its pretext.
wars.note: The Masinissa page dates Oroscopa 151; the Third Punic War page's lead dates the campaign to 149. The page names none of the land in dispute.

wars.name: Third Punic War
wars.outcome: Utica went over to Rome (149), the Romans landed and besieged Carthage; Scipio Aemilianus took sole command (147) and assaulted the city in spring 146; Carthage was destroyed and its territory became the Roman province of Africa.

certainty.note: Ancient frontiers throughout: the African interior, the Libyan coast and the Numidian frontier were never surveyed. Treaty lines are the exceptions: the Halycas river in Sicily (367, 339, 306), the Ebro in Iberia (226-218) and the 201 treaty confining Carthage to Africa, but the pages give no coordinates for any of them.

notes:
CLIOPATRIA ROW: one row, -650..-145, 29 shapes. It starts 164 years after the foundation (814 BC) and ends a year late (the city fell in spring 146). New keyframes: -814 (the city), -615 (colonies added), -306, -261, -254, -252 (Sicily, from the 306 treaty and the Roman conquest), -237 (Sardinia and Corsica out, Andalusia in). Eleven shapes are adjusted: -630, -404, -307, -256, -239, -218 (French cells of Hannibal's march), -216/-212/-208/-206 (Italy removed, drawn by contest events), -210 (29 Peloponnesian cells that no page supports), -203 (Syphax's Numidian kingdom), -202 (Balearics), -164 (years).
ITALY: Cliopatria draws Hannibal's whole Italian campaign as Carthaginian land (up to 426 cells, Po valley to Bruttium). The dossier removes it and records one contest zone for 218-203 (contest_start November 218 on arrival in Cisalpine Gaul, contest_end -203 at confidence 1); the Roman Republic dossier (eu-03) has the same pair of dates plus losses of Capua and Tarentum. Rule 6 gives the blend.
COLONIES: the Phoenicia page says the western colonies passed to Carthage in the 7th century; Cliopatria's Phoenician Colonies row ends -616 and Carthage's shape stays Tunisia-only to -501. The dossier bridges with a confidence-1 gain at -616 and keyframe -615. The specific pages say later: Sardinia c. 510 (History of Sardinia), the Sardinian expedition of the 520s and the 509 treaty (Magonid page), Gades after Tyre's fall in 573 (Cadiz page), and the Ancient Carthage infobox puts independence from Tyre in the mid-6th century. A gap-filler should decide which of these governs.
DISAGREEMENTS BETWEEN PAGES: Sardinia and Corsica pass to Rome in 238 (History of Sardinia, the Roman Republic dossier) or 237 (First Punic War, Mercenary War 'probably'); the dossier uses 237. The Ancient Carthage lead says Carthage held southern and eastern Iberia and Corsica by 300 BC, against the Barcid pages (237). The Magonid page dates the republic to both 480 and 308. Akragas fell 262 or 261 and was retaken 255 or 254 (First Punic War). Oroscopa is 151 (Masinissa) or 149 (Third Punic War lead). Hannibal was recalled in 204 (Second Punic War page) or left Italy in 203 (Hannibal page prose, Cliopatria and the Roman dossier): 203 is used, at confidence 2.
NOT ON THE PAGES OPENED (left to Cliopatria's shape, confidence 1 or verdict ok with 'unverified'): the founding of Carthago Nova c. 228; the Balearics before 201; the date of the Corsican acquisition (bridged at -384, confidence 1); the 75 Catalan and north-bank cells of -218; the seizures of Emporia and the Great Plains by Masinissa; the exact Libyan, Algerian and Moroccan losses of -197 (the 201 treaty took 'some of its African' territories, unnamed); the early territory of the city before -500; the Tunisian hinterland (410 per the Ancient Carthage page).
REBELS: the Mercenary War rebels held Tunis, Utica, Hippo and Leptis Parva for up to three years; they are written as the rebel state mercenary-rebels (slug from the name 'Mercenary rebels'), counterpart of the 241, 239 and 238 events.
SYRACUSE AND THE GREEK CITIES: the Sicilian counterparts are syracuse (Dionysius, Agathocles) and greek-city-states (Selinus, Himera, Akragas, Gela, Camarina); the Cliopatria Greek City-States row is eu-01's and may be split.
PAGE BUDGET: nine pages were opened for this state (Ancient Carthage, Sicilian Wars, the three Punic Wars, Hamilcar Barca, Magonid dynasty, Masinissa, Pyrrhus); Phoenicia, History of Sardinia, Mercenary War and Cadiz were opened for the neighbouring dossiers and are cited here for the events they date. Shapes before -500 and the small Sicilian steps of -272 and -264 stay 'unverified: page budget'.
GAZETTEER: places used by coordinates because the gazetteer lacks them: Utica, Hippo Diarrhytus (Bizerte), Leptis Parva (Lamta), Akragas, Selinous (Selinunte), Heraclea Minoa, Thermae (Termini Imerese), Saguntum, Aspis (Kelibia). Regions used: Andalusia, Murcia, Cisalpine Gaul, Apulia, Basilicata, Calabria, Campania, Africa Proconsularis, Balearic Islands, Hispania (all in regions.jsonl).
